hero.title: Enterprise-grade ad automation shouldn't belong only to clients spending millions a year

whySwitch.title: Why agencies move from Smartly to Cluega AI

items.title: A cost structure that grows out of the agency's business model
items.body: Smartly's platform fee is a fixed cost stacked on media budget — payable whether the ads perform or not, on top of an annual contract and onboarding fee. Cluega AI's fully managed mode takes a share of actual ad spend (4%→2.5%→1.5%, decreasing with scale) and includes the tokens, images, video and optimisation along the way: the client pays one predictable performance fee, and the agency's own pricing model grows directly on top of it.

items.title: With large brands, data security is the ticket into the pitch
items.body: The question agencies get asked most when serving large brands: "Will my ad data be used to train models? Will it get mixed with other clients?" Cluega offers private-hosted single-tenant storage (ClickHouse deployment) with local data residency: ad data never crosses tenants, is never distilled into any large-model training, and every access is logged for audit. Take that architecture into a pitch and security review stops being the reason you lose the account — it becomes the reason you win it.

items.title: Attribution that reaches private-domain sales, so agencies can show "true ROAS"
items.body: A huge share of the world's sales happen inside WhatsApp／LINE／Zalo conversations — Smartly's world stops at what the platform reports. Cluega connects e-commerce sales data from TikTok Shop／Amazon／Shopify on one side and uses private-domain IM attribution to push DM sales back to campaign and creative on the other: the report an agency hands its client upgrades from "platform conversions" to "true sales ROAS", and that is a structural difference in renewal rates.

items.title: We don't sell you a tool — we serve your clients with you
items.body: Smartly sells platform licences; landing and customisation are on the agency. Cluega AI stands shoulder to shoulder with agencies in serving clients: bespoke enterprise Skills tailored to the client's industry and processes — from a single workflow to autonomous multi-agent long flows, bought once and owned by the client on delivery. We believe marketing in this era isn't a contest of who has more tools, but of who can fuse the fragmented data scattered across ads, commerce, private domains and CRM into a core moat nobody else can take away.

steps: AI identifies pain points, keeps engaging

cache.bubble: The Meta ad audience seems fatigued—today the tumbler's CTR fell below 1% and ROAS dropped to 1.2. The campaign is still running. How do we save it now?
cache.sol1Text: immediately turn off the 2 worst-performing old image-text ads with frequency above 3.5 today, and shift 30% of budget to backup "unboxing short-video" creatives.
cache.sol2Text: check custom audiences, make sure "buyers from the past 30 days" are strictly excluded, and widen the pool by scaling the Lookalike ratio from 1% to 3%–5%.
cache.sol3Text: if CPM (cost per thousand impressions) still hasn't come down by 4 PM, the auction is overheated—immediately cut this campaign's budget by 50% and launch a new one running "add to cart" to warm up.

pancake.body: You serve global enterprise clients with ample monthly budgets concentrated inside the Meta／Google ecosystem, your focus is large-scale dynamic creative templates and a cross-platform media hub, and you can live with annual contracts and enterprise thresholds.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you might want to know before you reach out to our team.

items.q: We're a small-to-mid agency managing under $50K／month — is this a fit?
items.a: It is. Smartly's contract threshold usually only pays off above $20K／month in spend; Cluega AI's self-serve plan starts at $99／month, fully managed starts at a 4% share and the rate falls as scale grows, and agency plans can additionally be negotiated on managed volume.

items.q: How does the fully managed share differ from Smartly's platform fee?
items.a: Smartly's platform fee is a fixed cut, with creative and staffing costs for running the ads billed separately; Cluega's share covers everything — token consumption, image and video generation, and buying decisions during the managed period are all included, with nothing deducted on top. The client pays one "ad spend × share" line, and the bill is entirely predictable.

items.q: Can we use self-serve only, without handing over account management?
items.a: Yes. Self-serve is billed in credits (1 credit＝$0.001, transparently anchored), and asking the AI for a single task — produce a creative, write copy, adjust an audience — runs on credits; when you're ready, enable fully managed account by account. The two tracks are mutually exclusive and never stack.

items.q: How are security and permissions guaranteed across multiple client accounts?
items.a: Every client account runs its own AAIGS tiering: maturity M0–M5 determines AI authorisation T0–T3, new accounts start with low authorisation and are granted more as data accumulates; every AI decision carries an audit log, and manually operated campaigns don't count toward the share.

items.q: Large-brand clients require data to stay in-country and out of model training — can you meet that?
items.a: Yes, and this is exactly Cluega's standard answer for large brands. Under any plan, ad data is never used for cross-tenant model training; for brands with high security and data-sovereignty requirements, you can add a private-hosted single-tenant ClickHouse deployment supporting local data residency and compliance add-ons (such as PDPL), with monitoring, redundancy and audit logs included — the AI uses your data to buy media for you, but your data belongs only ever to you.

items.q: How does bespoke enterprise Skill work as a collaboration?
items.a: The agency brings the client's requirements, and Cluega assesses the scenario, builds and delivers with you: from a standard Skill for a single workflow, to an advanced Skill integrating across systems, to flagship long flows with autonomous multi-agent orchestration — quoted once by complexity, owned outright on payment, with no annual fee. Skills keep benefiting from model updates on the platform, and the client's fragmented data settles into a marketing asset of their own — something an agency can deliver and a pure tool vendor cannot.
